summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 162% to INR314 crore and PAT 118% to INR44 crore, helped by the CrudeChem (CCT) acquisition.
summary.overview: Fineotex reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR314 crore, up 162% YoY, with PAT of INR44 crore versus INR20 crore a year earlier, driven by the newly acquired US oilfield chemicals business CrudeChem Technologies Group (CCT). International revenue rose to 70% of the mix and ROIC was stated at 31%. Management said Q4 is the base for future growth, is doubling CCT's manufacturing capacity, and targets a $200 million CCT revenue run-rate before 2028 and a blended EBITDA of 18-20%. Non-CCT textile volumes were said to be recovering, with textile specialty up about 8% YoY in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Increased significantly, no prior figure given
Cited by analyst; not disputed by management

segments.name: Oil & Gas specialty chemicals (CCT)
segments.commentary: Management said oil specialty chemicals were about 55-60% of Q4 revenue by value, with annualised Q4 run-rate of about $90-100 million. Capacity is being doubled at CCT, with Midland expansion and new machinery ordered.

segments.name: Specialty textile chemicals (Fineotex, Ambernath)
segments.commentary: Textile share of total revenue fell to about 35-36%, though textile revenue grew in value. Textile specialty volumes were up about 8% YoY in Q4 and about 15% in volume per a later clarification.

segments.name: FMCG and hygiene chemicals
segments.commentary: No segment-specific figures were given on the call; management said other industries grew faster than textile.

guidance_outlook: CCT revenue target of $200 million, now brought forward to before 2028 from an earlier 2030 timeline; management declined to give FY27/FY28 revenue guidance.
Blended consolidated EBITDA target of 18-20%, which management said could be reflected within FY27; CCT EBITDA comfortably around 15%.
Stake: founders to sell a further 25% of CCT to Fineotex in January 2028, taking the holding to about 79-80% (currently about 53%).
Analyst-framed scale-up to INR3,000 crore top line in 3-4 years was not refuted; management said it would be surprised if not reached.
Working capital tolerated up to 90 days; management said current 79 days is at par with industry.
capex_capacity: CCT capacity doubling in progress; a large order of machines placed, with installation expected within a couple of weeks of the call.
Fineotex spent about $7 million capex post-acquisition and extended about $7 million more to CCT for further investment.
Ambernath plant utilisation about 60-62% in Q4 FY26, expected to rise in Q1.
Subsidiary in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, was set up for a plant but has not started; Middle East options are being explored, including inorganic routes.
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry environment was stable with healthy demand; FY26 textile exports grew 2.1% YoY to $3.16 trillion (as stated on the call), with the India-US trade deal and UK and EU trade frameworks cited as tailwinds.
North American oilfield demand is rising, with Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela cited as new areas; management said the addressable market is about $3.5-4 billion.
Pricing: management said raw material cost increases are passed on to customers; inventory is held for 1-2 months. Logistics and freight costs were a challenge in Q4 and April.

Competitive moat is described as technical services, last-mile delivery, weather-specific customisation and customer qualification taking around 2 years; management said wallet share could rise 5x with existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is $200 million CCT revenue expected by FY28, and what EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the annualised Q4 run-rate is $90-100 million and it is confident of $200 million before 2028; EBITDA is expected to be comfortably around 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CCT revenue guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward-looking numbers and said Q4 FY26 is the base set for going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What blended consolidated EBITDA is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a blended 18-20%, with the Fineotex operations historically at 18-28% EBITDA, and said this could be reflected within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CCT stake roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: The founders have agreed to sell a further 25% by January 2028, taking Fineotex to about 79-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and cash flow impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is about 79 days, with management saying up to 90 days is acceptable. Management said the reported operating cash flow was reduced by a one-time acquisition-related entry in the accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What are CrudeChem's Q4 numbers and steady-state revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CrudeChem Q4 revenue was approximately INR165-170 crore. Management agreed that a steady-state top line of INR600-650 crore was easily achievable, with no seasonality in the business.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for revenue of INR3,000 crore in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth plus CCT and Ambernath could reach 3-4x current scale, and it would be surprised if INR3,000 crore was not touched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material and pricing situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost increases are passed on to customers, with no contracts, and the worst of the logistics disruption is behind them. It gave no quantified basket-level price change.

risks_watch: Revenue targets (USD 200 million by 2028, INR3,000 crore in 3-4 years) rest on management assertions with no formal guidance.
Cash flow: reported operating cash flow was negative for FY26 due to acquisition-related accounting, and working capital is elevated at 79 days.
Raw material and freight costs remain volatile; management says the worst is behind but April required inventory and pricing reset.
Capex and funding for CCT doubling plus the further 25% stake purchase due January 2028.
Related-party and UAE subsidiary plant status not clear; Middle East plans remain unspecified.
Analyst questions on CCT's Q4 figures were answered only approximately; detailed CCT financial disclosure to be taken up via investor relations.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on CCT growth and margins, with forward targets stated as easily achievable. Evasive on specific FY27 and FY28 guidance, repeatedly declining numbers and giving approximate CrudeChem figures.
key_quotes: I am very confident that the team will be able to deliver a $200 million business in the coming times.
So, I would not be able to share any forward-looking statements here.
So I can easily envisage that 18% to 20% blended should be easy, should be achievable by us.
